_nota: El inglés del «Glosario de términos gramaticales de la lengua pali» de Bhikkhu Nandisena (recursos/glosario/nandisena.json). El español manda: es el suyo, y el inglés de cada entrada lo traduce entero, definición y ejemplos, sin añadir ni quitar. NO llega a la página mientras «adjudicado» sea false: generar_glosario.py lo comprueba entrada por entrada contra el español, pero no lo inyecta. La adjudicación va POR TANDA: cada tanda lleva su «adjudicado», «adjudicado_por» y «fecha», y cada entrada dice de qué tanda es; generar_glosario.py inyecta sólo las entradas de tandas adjudicadas. El «adjudicado» de arriba resume: true si alguna tanda lo está. Cotejo lado a lado, con la fuente de cada término, en docs/glosario/ingles-por-adjudicar.md.
_clave: La clave es el lema tal como lo imprime el Glosario. Cuando el mismo lema tiene más de una entrada —los homónimos «adhikaraṇa 1 / 2» y el «adhikāra» que sale dos veces sin número— la clave lleva «|N», con N el ordinal de aparición en nandisena.json (1, 2…). Las remisiones («akamma → v. akammaka») no tienen entrada aquí: no hay nada que traducir.
_prelacion: N-EN: el inglés del propio Nandisena — el Sandhi-kappa inglés (kaccayana/01-sandhi-kappa.en.md y el memo docs/ingles/memo-sandhi-en-glosario-y-desviaciones.md §2), su apéndice sobre «ca», y sus traducciones inglesas de Taddhita, Ākhyāta, Kibbidhāna y Uṇādi (docs/5 - …, 6 - …, 7- …, 8 - …).
IEBH: lo ya adjudicado en este repositorio — recursos/verbo/ingles.json (2026-09-01) y los casos e inflexiones de recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json.
Ñāṇamoli: «Grammatical Terms» (BPS 1994, rev. Ānandajoti 2014), recursos/glosario/terminos-nyanamoli.json, con página.
traducción: cuando ninguna de las tres da el término, se traduce el español de Nandisena y se dice.
_campos: «en» es la entrada entera en inglés. «termino» es la palabra o palabras inglesas del término principal, y «fuente» de dónde sale, con su lugar. «nota» avisa de lo que IEBH tiene que decidir: cuando una fuente de más autoridad dice otra cosa que el español del Glosario, o cuando el término choca con lo fijado en comun/glosario.md o en recursos/glosario/glosario-ingles.json.
_nota_borrador: Con «publicar_borrador»: true (IEBH, 2026-10-21), generar_glosario.py publica también el inglés de las tandas sin adjudicar, rotulado «draft» en cada entrada (en_borrador). Al adjudicar una tanda, sus entradas pierden el rótulo. Tandas 3-10 redactadas el 2026-10-21 con la misma prelación y el mismo cotejo.

1.veredicto: Las 14 notas del §3 del cotejo, tal como estaban redactadas: se publica el borrador sin cambios (sesión 57).

akathitakamma.en: lit., unspoken object; indirect object. It refers to the secondary object when the verb has two objects (dvikammaka). E.g., in the sentence "Bhagavā bhikkhū etad avoca", the Blessed One said this to the bhikkhus, "bhikkhū" is called akathitakamma, indirect object, and "etad", this, kathitakamma, direct object.
akathitakamma.nota: «el Bienaventurado» (en el impreso, «el Sublime»; sustituido por decisión del IEBH, sesión 58) se da como «the Blessed One», que es el inglés del propio Nandisena para Bhagavā (Ākhyāta, §415 y passim; invocación del Sandhi inglés).

akammaka.en: intransitive; without object; kamma in the ancient grammars is used to refer to the object of the verb. See also sakammaka; dvikammaka.

akkhara.en: phoneme; letter; syllable. There are 41 letters in the Pāḷi alphabet. The vowels are 8: 'a', 'ā', 'i', 'ī', 'u' 'ū', 'e', 'o'. And the consonants 33: 'k', 'kh', 'g', 'gh', 'ṅ'; 'c', 'ch', 'j', 'jh', 'ñ'; 'ṭ', 'ṭh', 'ḍ', 'ḍh', 'ṇ'; 't', 'th', 'd', 'dh', 'n'; 'p', 'ph', 'b', 'bh', 'm'; 'y', 'r', 'l', 'v', 's', 'h', 'ḷ', 'ṃ'.

akkhara-cintaka.en: grammarian; lit., one who thinks letters.

akkhara-kosalla.en: skillfulness with letters; mastery of letters.

akkhara-vipatti.en: misspelling; perversion of the meaning; error in the use of letters.
akkhara-vipatti.nota: N-EN, Sandhi §1, glosa «akkharavipattiyaṃ» como «deformity of letters». El Glosario español no dice eso («deletreo erróneo»), y aquí se sigue al Glosario; IEBH decide si el inglés debe alinear con el Sandhi inglés.

akhinimīlana.en: blink of an eye. The unit of measure of the short vowels, 'a', 'i', 'u'. See also accharāsaṅghāta.
akhinimīlana.nota: El lema impreso es «akhinimīlana» y la remisión desde accharāsaṅghāta dice «akkhinimīlana». No se toca: es del impreso.

aghosa.en: voiceless; voiceless (consonant). There are eleven voiceless consonants: 'k', 'kh'; 'c', 'ch'; 'ṭ', 'ṭh'; 't', 'th'; 'p', 'ph'; 's'. Cf. ghosa.
aghosa.nota: Ñāṇamoli p. 5 da «surd, unvoiced»; manda N-EN.

accantasaṃyoga.en: total connection of time or space. E.g., "māsaṃ adhīte", he studies for a whole month.
accantasaṃyoga.nota: Ñāṇamoli p. 13 da «direct governance (of acc. by transitive verb)», que es otra definición, no otra palabra. Se sigue al Glosario.

acchandānukkhaṇa.en: lit., without protecting the metre; without regard to the metre.

accharāsaṅghāta.en: snap of the fingers. This is considered a unit of measure (mattā). See also akkhinimīlana.

ajjatanī.en: the aorist in the Pāḷi language; past. It is used to express (1) the past directly experienced (paccakkha) and (2) the past not directly experienced (appaccakkha). The past expressed by this tense runs from today backwards; hence the name "ajjatanī".
ajjatanī.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («Aorist (ajjatanī)», «The past directly experienced (paccakkha)», «The past not directly experienced (appaccakkha)»); Ñāṇamoli pp. 7 y 13 coincide

ajjhesanā.en: consent; permission. One of the uses of the imperative (pañcamī) and potential (sattamī) verb.
ajjhesanā.nota: DUDA para IEBH: la página del verbo, ya adjudicada por el IEBH, da «Request (ajjhesanā)» / «Request, permission», y reserva «consent» para anumati. El Glosario español dice «consentimiento; permiso» para las dos. Se traduce lo que dice el Glosario; la discrepancia es de las fuentes, no de la traducción.

aññattha.en: lit., another meaning. One of the functions of the particle "na" when it forms a compound with another word. E.g., "a-byākata", undeclared.

aññapada.en: lit., another word. Technical term used to refer to "ya", "ta", "eta" and "ima". These pronouns are used in the resolution (viggaha) of relative compounds (bahubbīhi). E.g., "chinno hattho yassa so ti chinnahattho", cut is the hand of this one, he is (a man with a) cut hand. In this example, "yassa" is called "aññapada" and it is used to resolve the compound.
aññapada.fuente: traducción; «relative compound» para bahubbīhi es de Ñāṇamoli pp. 11 y 17 y de glosario-ingles.json (propuesta)

aññapadattha-padhāna.en: type of compound in which another word is predominant. It belongs to the group of relative compounds (bahubbīhi). See aññapada.
aññapadattha-padhāna.termino: compound in which another word is predominant

aḍḍhamattā.en: half a unit of measure; half a mora. See mattā and accharāsaṅghāta.

atagguṇasaṃviññāṇa.en: type of relative compound (bahubbīhi) in which what qualifies the meaning is not brought along when the meaning of the other word (aññapada) is brought. What qualifies the meaning is not included in the meaning of the other word. E.g., "bahudhanaṃ ānaya", bring (the man of) much wealth. Here, what qualifies, much wealth, is not brought when the man is brought. It is the opposite of tagguṇasaṃviññāṇa.
atagguṇasaṃviññāṇa.termino: (relative compound) in which the qualifier is not brought along

atīta-kāla.en: past tense; one of the verbal tenses. In the Rūpasiddhi it is mentioned as a synonym of the aorist tense (ajjatanī).

attanopada.en: middle or reflexive voice (lit. word for oneself); one of the two groups of verbal inflections (ākhyāta-vibhatti). The other group is called parassapada.
attanopada.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («Word for oneself; middle or reflexive voice (attanopada)»); N-EN Ākhyāta §407 escribe «word for itself»; Ñāṇamoli p. 8 coincide

atthantaraviññāpanatthaṃ.en: in order to make known another meaning.
atthantaraviññāpanatthaṃ.termino: in order to make known another meaning

attha-pūraṇa.en: lit., that completes or fills the meaning; a class of particles (nipāta). This class of particles denotes a meaning that has already been denoted by another word (or words), but it becomes a little more explicit. E.g., when one says "khattiyo brāhmaṇo vesso suddo", warrior, brahmin, merchant and servant, without the particle "ca", and "khattiyo ca brāhmaṇo ca vesso ca suddo ca", both sentences have the same meaning, but the use of the particle "ca" makes the meaning a little more explicit. This type of particle may be associated with a given inflection (vibhattiyutta) or dissociated from inflection (avibhattiyutta). See also pūraṇattha and pada-pūraṇa.
attha-pūraṇa.fuente: traducción; «particle» para nipāta es N-EN, Sandhi §51 (memo §2.1)

atthasambandha.en: unity of meaning; connection of meaning.

atthyattha-taddhita.en: secondary suffixes (taddhita) denoting possession (endowed with). These suffixes are secondary derivatives and belong to the category sāmañña-taddhita, general secondary derivative. The following suffixes belong to this category: ava, ala, ila, ika, ī, vī, ssī, vantu, mantu, a, tara, tama.
atthyattha-taddhita.fuente: N-EN, título del capítulo 5 («Secondary Derivative Chapter»); Ñāṇamoli p. 11 («general secondary derivative» para sāmaññataddhita, «denoting endowment, possession» para atthyattha)
atthyattha-taddhita.nota: glosario-ingles.json (propuesta sin adjudicar) da taddhita → «nominal derivative». N-EN dice «secondary derivative» y aquí manda N-EN; convendría alinear la propuesta.

adassana.en: lit., not being seen; absence. It is a term used to define lopa, elision.

adhikaraṇa|1.en: the seventh case; the locative case. See kāraka.
adhikaraṇa|1.fuente: IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, casos_en («locative»); Ñāṇamoli p. 13 («one kind of locative»)

adhikaraṇa|2.en: relation; relation of words in a sentence between which there is agreement, either as adjective and noun, as subject and predicate, or as two nouns in apposition.

adhikāra|1.en: relation of influence; authority; general rule. A rule that has influence over a certain number of following rules is called anu-vutti. There are three types of relation of influence: (1) lion's movement (sīha-gatika), (2) frog's movement (maṇḍūka-gatika) and (3) following the order (yathānupubbika).
adhikāra|1.nota: comun/glosario.md fija adhikāra → «aforismo regulativo» (Nāma §52) y glosario-ingles.json propone «governing aphorism». Esta entrada del Glosario define otra cosa —la relación de influencia— y se traduce tal cual; la segunda entrada, abajo, es la que casa con la norma.

adhikāratthaṃ.en: for the purpose of being a general rule.
adhikāratthaṃ.termino: for the purpose of being a general rule
adhikāratthaṃ.nota: N-EN, Ākhyāta §413 («Kāle» icc’ etaṃ adhikāratthaṃ veditabbaṃ): «It should be understood that “kāla” (time) is for the sake of following.» El Venerable traduce adhikāra por «following» en ese pasaje.

adhikāra|2.en: governing aphorism, of general application. See sutta.
adhikāra|2.fuente: glosario-ingles.json (propuesta sin adjudicar) para la norma «aforismo regulativo»

anabhihita-kamma.en: object not indicated. It is a synonym of avutta-kamma.

anādara.en: disregard. Genitive absolute. E.g. "rudato dārakassa pabbaji", (the father) went forth although his son was crying. Here the father disregarded (anādara) the fact that his son was crying (rudato dārakassa) and went forth (pabbaji).
anādara.nota: «renunció» (pabbaji) se da como «went forth», que es lo usual en inglés para pabbajati; si IEBH prefiere el calco «renounced», se cambia.

aniṭṭhappasaṅga.en: inclusion of what is not desired.
aniṭṭhappasaṅga.termino: inclusion of what is not desired

aniyamuddesa.en: the relative clause, also called "subordinate clause".

anukaḍḍhana.en: previous reference; grammatical attraction; dragging. This term is generally used to bring certain necessary terms from a previous aphorism into the aphorism in question.
anukaḍḍhana.fuente: N-EN, apéndice sobre «ca» (docs/fuentes/nandisena-apendice-sandhi-en.md) y Sandhi inglés, notas 12 y 29

anukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.en: for the purpose of bringing or dragging.

anukaraṇa.en: resemblance, similarity. "Ati- upasaggānukaraṇa", resembling the preposition 'ati'.
anukaraṇa.nota: El Glosario dice «preposición» para upasagga; la norma (comun/glosario.md) y N-EN §51 dicen «prefijo / prefix». Se traduce lo que dice el Glosario.

anuttasamuccaya.nota: Para samuccaya solo, N-EN (apéndice) dice «accumulating» y Ñāṇamoli p. 9 «conjunction (ca)». El Glosario español da «agrupación o colección», y se sigue al Glosario.

anupadiṭṭha.nota: N-EN, Sandhi §51, traduce «Anupadiṭṭhānaṃ» por «Of those that have not been shown» / «whose formations have not been shown». Es la misma idea con otra palabra; IEBH decide si el término va «not shown».

anubandha.en: indicatory letter; it is used to indicate grammatical operations such as the strengthening of a short vowel.
anubandha.fuente: N-EN, Taddhita §353 («the indicatory letter ‘ṇ’») y Ākhyāta, verso de apertura («elisions and indicatory letters»)

anumati.en: concession; consent; permission. One of the uses of the imperative (pañcamī) and potential (sattamī) verb.

anuvattati.en: verb used in the ancient grammars to indicate the continuation of a previous rule; that continues from a previous rule. Also anuvattate.

anuvattana-vutti.en: word or term coming from previous aphorisms.

anu-vutti.en: rule or aphorism that has influence over a certain number of following rules.
anu-vutti.termino: rule that has influence over the following rules

anussāra.fuente: N-EN deja niggahita sin traducir (Sandhi §8; memo §2.1); Ñāṇamoli p. 13 («the letter ṁ, the nasal»)

anekattha.en: having several meanings; secondary derivation suffixes denoting various meanings. They belong to the category of general secondary derivatives (sāmañña-taddhita). The following suffixes belong to this category: (ṇ)ika, (ṇ)a, ima, iya, tā, ālu, ka, maya.
anekattha.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 11 («of various meanings»); «general secondary derivative» p. 11

anekavacana.en: plural. It is a synonym of bahuvacana.

antaṭṭha.en: semivowel; lit., the letters at the end (of the grouped ones): 'y', 'r', 'l', 'v'. They are placed between the consonants and the vowels.

anvattha.en: that follows the meaning; in accordance with the true meaning. Cf. ruḷhī.

anvācaya.en: that connects a secondary action with the main action; coordination of two activities; one of the functions of the particle "ca". E.g., "dānañ ca dehi, sīlañ ca rakkhāhi", give alms and keep the precepts. Sad. explains this use of "ca" as the sphere of separate actions (bhinnakiriyāvisaya).

apaccattha.en: suffixes denoting lineage. They belong to the category of general secondary derivatives (sāmañña-taddhita). The following suffixes belong to this category: (ṇ)a, (ṇ)āyana, (ṇ)āna, (ṇ)eyya, (ṇ)ava, (ṇ)era.
apaccattha.nota: N-EN, Taddhita §344, traduce apacca por «offspring» («In the offspring there is ‘ṇa’»). El Glosario español dice «linaje»; se sigue al Glosario y se deja constancia.

apavāda.en: prevention; exception. It is the opposite of ussagga (Mogp. 242). According to Monier 52, it is "a special rule that takes precedence over a general rule".
apavāda.nota: Ñāṇamoli no lo registra. El Conspectus de Smith (7.3.2.1, p. 1146) da «une exception ⟨apavāda⟩» frente a «l'énoncé positif [utsarga]», que coincide con el Glosario.

apādāna.en: the fifth case; the ablative case. See kāraka.
apādāna.fuente: IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, casos_en («ablative»); Ñāṇamoli p. 7 («ablative (pañcamī: fifth)») coincide

apekkhākaraṇattha.en: for the purpose of referring (to the words mentioned before).

appaccakkha.en: lit., that is not perceptible through the senses; that has not been experienced; one of the uses of the verbal tenses ajjatanī, hiyyattanī and parokkhā
appaccakkha.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («The past not directly experienced (appaccakkha)»)
appaccakkha.nota: El Glosario español cierra la entrada sin punto final; se reproduce así.

appadhānaliṅga.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 6 («adjective (whose gender does not predominate)»)

appasiddha.en: not evident; non-existent. "Akāranto itthiliṅgasaddo appasiddho", the feminine word(s) ending in 'a' are not evident.

aphuṭṭha.en: non-occlusive. According to Sad. §16 this term is used to refer to the unaspirated consonants (sithila).
aphuṭṭha.nota: Ñāṇamoli p. 4 da «unaspirate» para sithila, que coincide con el Glosario.

abbhāsa.en: the first syllable of a reduplicated root. E.g., in "dadāti", (he/she) gives, the root is "dā", to give, which is reduplicated, and the vowel is shortened. The first syllable 'da' is called "abbhāsa".
abbhāsa.termino: first syllable of a reduplicated root
abbhāsa.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta («The previous (syllable) of the reduplicated root it is called “abbhāsa”»; «abbhāsa (previous reduplicated syllables)»)

abyaya.en: indeclinable. They are called indeclinables because they are not subject to changes; they are unmodifiable; they show no difference as to gender (liṅga), number (saṅkhyā) and inflection (vibhatti). There are 6 classes of indeclinables: (1) prefixes (upasagga), (2) particles (nipāta), (3) words ending in suffixes that are inflections (vibhatti-paccaya-pada), (4) adverbial compounds (abyayībhāva-samāsa), (5) words ending in indeclinable secondary suffixes (abyaya-taddhita-pada) and (6) words ending in the suffixes 'tvā', etc. (tvādi-paccayanta-pada).
abyaya.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 6 («indeclinable», bajo avyaya); «prefixes and particles» es N-EN, Sandhi §51
abyaya.nota: El español imprime «adverviales» y «pada)y»; se traduce «adverbial» y se separa el paréntesis, que son erratas de composición y no de contenido.

abyaya-taddhita.en: indeclinable numerals and adverbial secondary derivatives. The following suffixes belong to this category: kkhattuṃ, dhā, so, thā, thaṃ, tana, tra, ttha, hiṃ, haṃ, dā, dāni, dācanaṃ, ha, dha.
abyaya-taddhita.termino: indeclinable numerals and adverbial secondary derivatives
abyaya-taddhita.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 11 y 13 («indeclinable numerals and adverbs», bajo avyayataddhita); «secondary derivative» es N-EN, título del capítulo 5

abyayībhāva.en: Adverbial compound. The first member of this compound is an indeclinable and the second member is a noun. Generally this type of compound has the neuter singular ending. E.g., "nagarassa + upa" = "upanagaraṃ" (near the city). Also abyayībhāva-samāsa.
abyayībhāva.fuente: N-EN, Kibbidhāna («by way of adverbial compounds, secondary derivatives and verbs», glosando abyayībhāvasamāsataddhitākhyātato); Ñāṇamoli pp. 11 y 13 coincide

abhidheyya.en: the meaning expressed by a relative compound (bahubbīhi). E.g., the compound "āgatasamaṇo", lit., a monk having come, when it is a relative compound means something different from its components; in this example, "saṃghārāmo", monastery of the Order. Thus "āgatasamaṇo" means: the monastery of the Order to which the monk has come. The compound "saṃghārāmo" is called "abhidheyya", the meaning expressed by the relative compound "āgatasamaṇo".
abhidheyya.fuente: traducción; «relative compound» para bahubbīhi es de Ñāṇamoli pp. 11 y 17 y de glosario-ingles.json
abhidheyya.nota: El español imprime «babubbīhi»; se traduce bahubbīhi, que es errata de composición. Y CHOCA CON SMITH: en el Conspectus (6.0.3, p. 1134) abhidheyya es el Significado en general, «le Signifié», y la ficha de allí ya lo marca como conflicto. Se traduce lo que dice el Glosario.

abhidheyyaliṅga.nota: Ñāṇamoli p. 6 da «noun (whose gender predominates)» bajo padhānaliṅga, no bajo abhidheyyaliṅga. Se sigue al Glosario.

abhidheyyaliṅgavacana.en: having the (same) number and gender as the word denoted. This is one of the characteristics of relative compounds (bahubbīhi). The compound "āgatasamaṇo" has the same number (singular) and gender (masculine) as "saṃghārāmo", the word the compound denotes.
abhidheyyaliṅgavacana.termino: having the same number and gender as the word denoted

abhihita-kamma.en: indicated object. It is a synonym of vutta-kamma.

amādi-tappurisa.en: name for all the determinative compounds (tappurisa) except the numerical (digu) and adjectival (kammadhāraya) compounds. Cf. ubhe-tappurisa.
amādi-tappurisa.fuente: traducción; «determinative compound» para tappurisa, «numerical» para digu y «adjectival compound» para kammadhāraya son de Ñāṇamoli pp. 10, 14 y 16
amādi-tappurisa.nota: Ñāṇamoli traduce tappurisa por «dependent determinative compound»; el Glosario español dice sólo «determinativo» y se sigue al Glosario. Smith imprime «⟨amādi⟩» angular en la p. 1124 (sesión 56).

amādipara-tappurisa.en: type of determinative compound whose last member is a word ending in 'aṃ', etc.
amādipara-tappurisa.termino: determinative compound whose last member ends in aṃ, etc.

ayuttattha-samāsa.en: type of compound whose members are not linked in meaning. E.g., "apunageyyā gāthā", a verse not recited again; "alavaṇbhojī", one who does not eat salt. In these compounds the negative particle is not linked in meaning with the following member but with the last member of the compound.
ayuttattha-samāsa.termino: compound whose members are not linked in meaning
ayuttattha-samāsa.nota: El español imprime «alavaṇbhojī», sin la a de lavaṇa; se reproduce tal cual porque es el ejemplo del impreso y no se enmienda.

alutta-samāsa.en: type of compound in which the ending of the first member is not elided. E.g. "pabhaṅ karoti" = "pabhaṅkaro", making light, the sun.
alutta-samāsa.termino: compound with the ending not elided
alutta-samāsa.fuente: glosario-ingles.json (propuesta sin adjudicar): «compound with the [inflection] not elided»
alutta-samāsa.nota: Smith lematiza «alutta⟨vibhattika⟩samāsa» (5.2, p. 1123) con el angular de Moggallāna: revisión-de-las-i.md §5.20.

alopa-tappurisa.en: type of determinative compound in which the ending of the first member is not elided. See alutta-samāsa.
alopa-tappurisa.termino: determinative compound with the ending not elided

avaṇṇa.fuente: glosario-ingles.json (propuesta sin adjudicar), idéntica; N-EN Taddhita §405 da «the letter ‘a’» para akāra
avaṇṇa.nota: El español imprime «ā'» sin la comilla de apertura; se cierra en inglés, que es errata de composición.

avadhāraṇapubbapada-kammadhāraya.en: type of compound in which the first member restricts the second member. E.g., "guṇo eva dhanaṃ" = "guṇadhanaṃ", rich in virtue; lit., virtue itself is (his) wealth.
avadhāraṇapubbapada-kammadhāraya.termino: adjectival compound whose first member restricts
avadhāraṇapubbapada-kammadhāraya.fuente: traducción; «adjectival compound» para kammadhāraya es de Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 14; «limiting (avadhāraṇa)» es N-EN, Kibbidhāna, y «to restrict» glosario-ingles.json

avayava.en: part; constituent; one of the two uses of the genitive (partitive genitive). E.g., "brāhmaṇānaṃ so paṇḍito", he is wise among the brahmins.
avayava.nota: Ñāṇamoli lo registra sólo como constituyente de compuesto; el Glosario lo da como uso del genitivo. Se sigue al Glosario.

avibhattiyutta.en: not associated with inflection. It refers to a class of particles (nipāta) that is not associated with any inflection. See attha-pūraṇa.
avibhattiyutta.fuente: traducción; «inflection» para vibhatti es glosario-ingles.json y la página del verbo (IEBH)

avivaṭa.en: (mouth) not fully open; it refers to the way of pronouncing the letter 'ṃ'.

avutta-kattu.en: lit., unmentioned agent. E.g., in "ahinā daṭṭho naro", a man bitten by a snake, "ahinā" is called "avutta-kattā". See vutta-kattu.
avutta-kattu.nota: El español dice «subjeto no mencionado» (sic, por «sujeto»). Se traduce «agent» y no «subject» porque kattu es el agente de la construcción pasiva —«ahinā» es el instrumental—, y así lo entiende Ñāṇamoli p. 8 (kattukāraka, «active voice»). Si el IEBH prefiere el calco «subject», se cambia.

avutta-kamma.en: lit., unmentioned object. E.g., in "puriso rūpaṃ passati", the man sees a form, "rūpaṃ", form, is called "avutta-kamma". It is a synonym of anabhihita-kamma. Cf. vutta-kamma.
avutta-kamma.fuente: traducción, como anabhihita-kamma («object not indicated», tanda 1)

avuddhika.en: weak or no strengthening of the root; it refers to a sub-group of roots in which the first vowel of the root is not strengthened.
avuddhika.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 13 («weak strengthening of root in vowel gradation»); «strengthening (vuddhi)» es N-EN, Taddhita §353 y Kibbidhāna

avyatta-sadda.nota: El español imprime «abyatta-sadda .» con espacio antes del punto; se cierra.

asaṃyoga.en: non-conjunct (consonant); simple consonant. Also asaññoga. Cf. saṃyoga.
asaṃyoga.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §41 («conjunct consonant» para saṃyoga; memo §2.1) y Kibbidhāna §973 («of not a conjunct consonant», glosando asaṃyogantassa)

asabba-dhātuka.en: the four verbal inflections that are not placed after all roots. This term refers to those conjugations in which 'i' is optionally inserted before the verbal inflection suffix. They are the following: 1) perfect (parokkhā), 2) aorist (ajjatanī), 3) future (bhavissantī), 4) conditional (kālātipatti).
asabba-dhātuka.termino: asabbadhātuka (conjugations in which 'i' is optionally inserted)
asabba-dhātuka.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («In the conjugations that follow, called “not all roots” (asabbadhātuka), ‘i’ is optionally inserted before the verbal inflection suffix»); los cuatro tiempos, IEBH, misma página
asabba-dhātuka.nota: El español escribe «conditional» en inglés y «Perfecto» con mayúscula; se normaliza. La página del verbo, ya adjudicada, traduce el nombre como «not all roots»; el Glosario no lo traduce y aquí tampoco. 2026-09-27: IEBH antepone «las cuatro inflexiones verbales que no se colocan después de todas las raíces»; el inglés lo sigue (traducción).

asamāhāra-digu.en: Non-collective numerical determinative compound. This type of compound does not express the totality but the objects individually. The first member is a numeral. It has plural ending. E.g., "tayo + bhavā" = "tibhavā" (the three planes of existence).
asamāhāra-digu.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 16 («numerical determinative compound» para digu; «individual plural termination» para asamāhāra)

asamāhāra-dvanda.en: individual copulative compound. This type of compound does not express the totality but the objects individually. It has plural ending. E.g., "samaṇā ca brāhamaṇā ca" = "samaṇabrāhmaṇā" (monks and brahmins).
asamāhāra-dvanda.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 16 («copulative compound» para dvanda) y glosario-ingles.json (propuesta), idéntica; «individual» es Ñāṇamoli p. 10
asamāhāra-dvanda.nota: El español imprime «brāhamaṇā» en el ejemplo, errata de composición que el compuesto de al lado (samaṇabrāhmaṇā) delata; se reproduce tal cual, como alavaṇbhojī en ayuttattha-samāsa, porque el ejemplo es del impreso y no se enmienda.

asarūpa.en: dissimilar. The vowels 'a' and 'ā' are sarūpa, similar; likewise 'i', 'ī'; 'u', 'ū'. Therefore 'a' is dissimilar from 'i', 'ī', 'u', 'ū', 'e', 'o'. Cf. sarūpa. See asavaṇṇa.
asarūpa.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §13 y nota 19 («similar / dissimilar»; memo §2.1)
asarūpa.nota: El español imprime «'u, 'ū'» con una comilla de menos; se cierra.

asavaṇṇa.en: without a similar letter; dissimilar. The vowels 'a', 'ā'; 'i', 'ī'; 'u', 'ū' are savaṇṇa, with a similar letter; the vowels 'e' and 'o' are asavaṇṇa, without a similar letter.
asavaṇṇa.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §14 («dissimilar»; memo §2.1, que avisa de que N-EN usa la misma palabra para asarūpa y asavaṇṇa)

assapada-viggaha.en: type of compound whose resolution is not by means of its own words but by means of other words. E.g., the compound "upa-nagaraṃ", near the city, is explained as "nagarassa samīpaṃ". Another e.g., "paccate pāko", cooking (paccate) means cooking (pāko). In this case "pāko", a primary derivative (kita) used as a verbal noun (bhāva-sādhana), is explained by using a verb (paccate). The opposite is sapada-viggaha.
assapada-viggaha.termino: compound resolved by means of other words
assapada-viggaha.fuente: traducción; «verbal noun» y «definition by way of state (bhāvasādhana)» son de Ñāṇamoli pp. 12, 15 y 17
assapada-viggaha.nota: El español imprime «bhāva-sadhāna» (sic, por sādhana); se traduce bhāva-sādhana.

assutālāpa.en: one who has never heard human language.
assutālāpa.termino: one who has never heard human language

ākhyāta.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («The verb · ākhyāta»); N-EN, Kibbidhāna («verbs») y Ñāṇamoli p. 4 coinciden

ākhyāta-vibhatti.en: verbal inflection; verb ending. The group of verbal inflections begins with 'ti' (tyādayo).

āgama.en: insertion; inclusion of a vowel or consonant; augment.
āgama.nota: El español imprime «inclusión de de una vocal»; se quita la repetición. Y el Conspectus de Smith usa āgama TAMBIÉN por «tradición» (5.3.3.1, 7.1.1.1): las fichas de allí lo marcan como conflicto y piden ensanchar esta entrada; la decisión sigue siendo del IEBH.

āṇatti.en: command; precept; requirement. One of the uses of the imperative (pañcamī) verb.

ādesa.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §17 y §44 («substitution», «is substituted by»; memo §2.1)

ādesi.en: that which is substituted. See ādesiṭṭhāna.

ādesiṭṭhāna.en: place of substitution; letter that is substituted. E.g. in "me ayaṃ" = "my ayaṃ". The letter 'e' in "me" is called ādesi, the original form, that which is substituted. The letter 'y' is called ādesa, the substitute.
ādesiṭṭhāna.nota: El ejemplo «me ayaṃ» = «my ayaṃ» va como lo imprime el Glosario, con la forma intermedia y no la juntura myāyaṃ.

āmeḍita.en: repetition. It is used to give emphasis (very), distribution (with pronouns and indeclinables) or to express intense emotion.
āmeḍita.nota: Smith lo imprime «āmeṇḍita» con ṇ (6.1.3.1, p. 1137) y «[āmreḍitasamāsa]» entre corchetes (5.2.5, p. 1126); el Glosario da āmeḍita con ḍ. Es grafía, no término; no se toca.

ālapana.en: the vocative; addressing someone; speaking while looking at the other person. Also sambodhana.
ālapana.fuente: IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, inflexiones_en («vocative (ālapana)»); glosario-ingles.json y Ñāṇamoli p. 7 coinciden

ālapana-vacana.fuente: IEBH, como la anterior; Ñāṇamoli p. 14 («vocative case»)

āsiṭṭha.en: blessing; wish. One of the uses of the imperative (pañcamī) verb.

itaritara.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 14 («dvanda with plural ending»); «copulative compound» pp. 10 y 16

itarītarayoga.en: mutual connection; one of the functions of the particle "ca". E.g., " cando ca sūriyo ca", the moon and the sun.
itarītarayoga.nota: N-EN, en su apéndice sobre «ca», no nombra itarītarayoga entre las funciones (dragging, collecting, accumulating, delimiting, smoothness of speech): es la lista de la Rūpasiddhi, no la de Kaccāyana. El español imprime «Ej.," cando» con el espacio dentro de la comilla; se reproduce tal cual, que es lo que el generador comprueba.

itthambhūta-vacana.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 7 («ablative of likeness», bajo itthambhūtavacana)

itthambhūtākkhyānatthe upayogavacanaṃ.en: accusative of specification of state. E.g., in the sentence: "Taṃ kho pana bhagavantaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato", "taṃ kho pana bhagavantaṃ" is accusative of specification of state.
itthambhūtākkhyānatthe upayogavacanaṃ.fuente: traducción; «accusative» para upayoga es IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, casos_en («accusative»), como upayoga, y Ñāṇamoli pp. 7 y 14

itthiliṅga.fuente: N-EN, Taddhita §391 («by way of feminine, masculine and neuter gender», glosando itthipumanapuṃsakaliṅgato) y Kibbidhāna §553 («when the feminine gender is meant»); Ñāṇamoli p. 6 coincide
itthiliṅga.nota: El español imprime «V. liṅga 1 .» con espacio antes del punto; se cierra.

itthiliṅga-rūpa.en: form in the feminine gender; nominal stem in the feminine gender.
itthiliṅga-rūpa.fuente: traducción; «feminine gender» es N-EN, como itthiliṅga

ivaṇṇa.fuente: traducción, paralela a la norma avaṇṇa (comun/glosario.md «las letras ‘a’ y ‘ā’»; glosario-ingles.json «the letters ‘a’ and ‘ā’»)
ivaṇṇa.nota: N-EN, Taddhita §405, dice «‘i’, ‘ī’ are the character ‘i’ (ivaṇṇo)»: «character», no «letters». Se sigue al Glosario español y a la norma de avaṇṇa (fijada «según Nandisena»); IEBH decide si el inglés debe alinear con el Taddhita inglés. Lo mismo vale para uvaṇṇa.

īsaṃphuṭṭha.en: the letters 'y', 'r', 'l', 'v'. Semivowel (lit. little contact; produced with little contact).

uccāraṇattha.en: useful for pronunciation, necessary for pronunciation. The letter 'a' in the Burmese Pāḷi alphabets, etc., is necessary for the pronunciation of the consonants; the letter 'a' is included in the representation of each of the consonants.

uttama-purisa.en: the first person ("ahaṃ", I, "mayaṃ", we); lit. the most important person.
uttama-purisa.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §408 («first person (uttamapurisa)»); IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («First (uttama)»), glosario-ingles.json y Ñāṇamoli p. 8 coinciden

uttaratra.en: further on; below (in a book or manuscript).

uttara-padattha-padhāna.en: type of compound in which the last member is predominant. It may be an adjectival compound (kammadhāraya), a numerical compound (digu) or a determinative compound (tappurisa).
uttara-padattha-padhāna.termino: compound in which the last member is predominant
uttara-padattha-padhāna.fuente: traducción, como aññapadattha-padhāna (tanda 1); «adjectival compound», «numerical» y «determinative compound» son de Ñāṇamoli pp. 10, 14 y 16

upakaraṇa-saññā.en: useful term; accessory technical term. E.g., lopa, elision; āgama, insertion; etc.
upakaraṇa-saññā.fuente: traducción; «elision» (lopa) e «insertion» (āgama) son N-EN, Sandhi §12 y §35-37 (memo §2.1)

upaññāsa.en: exordium; introductory part of a treatise or discourse. One of the uses of the particle 'ca'. Also vākyārambha.

upadha.en: name of the penultimate letter of a word. E.g., the root "gaha" is divided into two syllables 'ga' and 'ha', the letter 'a' of 'ga' is called "upadha".
upadha.fuente: N-EN, Uṇādi §629 («Optionally there is ‘e’ of the letter ‘a’ that is the penultimate of the root ‘gaha’», glosando «Gahass’ upadhass’ e vā»)

upapada.en: adjacent word, nearby word, preceding word. The definition of this term (Rū §46) is "upoccāritaṃ padaṃ, upapadaṃ", "upapada" is the word that is pronounced contiguously. E.g., in the compound "kumbha- kāro", "kumbha", water pot, is called upapada, adjacent word. Also upapada-samāsa and kitanta-samāsa.
upapada.nota: comun/glosario.md fija upapada → «miembro precedente» (Nāma §79) y glosario-ingles.json propone «preceding member». El Glosario da en primer lugar «palabra adyacente» y sólo en tercero «palabra precedente»; se traduce tal cual. IEBH decide si el término inglés debe ser el de la norma. Además: el ejemplo entre comillas «kumbha- kāro» lleva un espacio tras el guion y se reproduce tal cual (es lo que el generador comprueba); en «upapada- samāsa», fuera de comillas, el espacio se cierra.

upapada-tappurisa.en: verbal dependent determinative compound. E.g. "kumbha-kāro", maker of water pots.
upapada-tappurisa.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 10 («verbal dependent determinative compound», bajo upapadatappurisa)

upamāna.en: simile; comparison. As a technical term it means that with which the other thing is compared. In "saṅkho viya paṇḍaro", white like a conch, "saṅkho", conch, is called "upamāna" and "paṇḍaro", white, is called upameyya, that which is compared.
upamāna.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §436 («Why it is said “upamāna” (comparison)?»); glosario-ingles.json («comparison») coincide

upamāna-pubbapada.en: one of the 9 classes of relative compounds (bahubbīhi). It has as its first member a word of comparison. This compound is in the first and sixth inflection. E.g., "kāko viya suro ayaṃ iti kākasuro", this one is bold like a crow, therefore he is called "bold as a crow".
upamāna-pubbapada.termino: relative compound whose first member is a word of comparison
upamāna-pubbapada.fuente: traducción; «relative compound» para bahubbīhi es de Ñāṇamoli pp. 11 y 17 y de glosario-ingles.json; «comparison» para upamāna es N-EN, Ākhyāta §436
upamāna-pubbapada.nota: El ejemplo imprime «suro» (no «sūro»); se reproduce tal cual, porque el ejemplo es del impreso y no se enmienda.

upamānuttarapada-kammadhāraya.en: type of compound in which the last member is an analogy of the first member. E.g., "muni- sīho" = "sīho viya muni", a sage like a lion, lion-sage, epithet of the Buddha.
upamānuttarapada-kammadhāraya.termino: adjectival compound whose last member is an analogy
upamānuttarapada-kammadhāraya.fuente: traducción; «adjectival compound» para kammadhāraya es de Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 14
upamānuttarapada-kammadhāraya.nota: El ejemplo entre comillas «muni- sīho» lleva un espacio tras el guion; se reproduce tal cual, que es lo que el generador comprueba.

upameyya.en: that which is compared. See example in upamāna.

upayoga.en: the second case; the accusative case. See also upayoga-vacana, kāraka.
upayoga.fuente: IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, casos_en («accusative»), como apādāna (tanda 2); Ñāṇamoli pp. 7 y 14 («accusative (dutiyā: second)», «accusative case», bajo upayogavacana) coincide

upayoga-vacana.en: the accusative case; the second case. Also upayoga.
upayoga-vacana.fuente: IEBH, como la anterior; Ñāṇamoli p. 14 («accusative case»)

upasa.en: prefixed vowel; vowel used as a prefix.

upasagga.en: prefix. Prefixes are placed before roots, verbs and derivatives. They have 3 functions: (1) to change, (2) to conform and (3) to modify. Examples: (1) "gacchati", he/she goes. If the prefix ā is placed before it, "ā-gacchati", he/she comes. In this case the meaning is the opposite; (2) "tiṭṭho", to be standing. If the prefix pati is placed before it, "pati-tiṭṭho", to be standing. In this case the meaning is not modified; (3) "harati", he / she carries. If the prefix pa is placed before it, "paharati", he / she strikes. In this case the meaning is modified. There are twenty prefixes: pa, parā, ni, nī, u, du, saṃ, vi, ava, anu, pari, adhi, abhi, pati, su, ā, ati, api, apa, upa.
upasagga.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §51 («prefixes»; memo §2.1); glosario-ingles.json y Ñāṇamoli p. 4 coinciden
upasagga.nota: El «7» que precede a la lista de los veinte prefijos es la llamada de la nota al pie 7 de la p. 9 del impreso (el orden de los prefijos en Rū. y en Sad.), que la extracción dejó en el texto; en el inglés se omite, como las llamadas 14 (pañcamī 1) y 17 (padesapariyosāna) de la tanda 6. IEBH decide si se quita también del español. Los ejemplos «tiṭṭho» y «pati-tiṭṭho» (así, y glosados ambos «estar parado») van tal cual.

upasaggānukaraṇa.en: resemblance to a prefix; that which resembles a prefix.

ubhaya-padattha-padhāna.en: type of aggregative compound (dvanda) in which both members are predominant.
ubhaya-padattha-padhāna.termino: compound in which both members are predominant
ubhaya-padattha-padhāna.nota: El español dice «compuesto agregativo (dvanda)»; comun/glosario.md fija dvanda → «compuesto copulativo» y glosario-ingles.json y Ñāṇamoli (pp. 10 y 16) dan «copulative compound». Se traduce «aggregative», como dice el Glosario; IEBH decide si se alinea con la norma.

ubhe-tappurisa.en: name given to the numerical (digu) and adjectival (kammadhāraya) compounds. Cf. amādi-tappurisa.
ubhe-tappurisa.termino: determinative compound of both kinds (digu and kammadhāraya)
ubhe-tappurisa.fuente: traducción, como amādi-tappurisa (tanda 2); «numerical» para digu y «adjectival compound» para kammadhāraya son de Ñāṇamoli pp. 10, 14 y 16

uvaṇṇa.fuente: traducción, paralela a la norma avaṇṇa, como ivaṇṇa
uvaṇṇa.nota: N-EN, Taddhita §405, dice «’u’ and ‘ū’ are the character ‘u’ (uvaṇṇo)». Véase la nota de ivaṇṇa.

ekapadasaṃyoga.en: a conjunct consonant that belongs to the same word as the preceding vowel. E.g., in "ettha", here, the conjunct consonant 'tth' belongs to the same word as the previous vowel 'e'. Cp. nānapadasaṃyoga.
ekapadasaṃyoga.termino: conjunct consonant in the same word
ekapadasaṃyoga.fuente: traducción; «conjunct consonant» para saṃyoga es N-EN, Sandhi §41 (memo §2.1)

ekamattā.en: one unit of measure; one mora (vowels 'a', 'i', 'u'). Also rassa, short. See mattā and accharāsaṅghāta.
ekamattā.fuente: traducción, como aḍḍhamattā (tanda 1); «mora» es N-EN, Kibbidhāna §602 («it has two moras»), y «short» para rassa es N-EN, Sandhi §4, y la norma

eka-vacana.fuente: N-EN, Kibbidhāna §571 («in the present singular and plural, ‘ti’ of the singular», glosando ekavacanabahuvacanesu ekavacanassa); IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («Singular (ekavacana)») y Ñāṇamoli p. 6 coinciden

okāsa.en: the seventh case; the locative case. See also kāraka.
okāsa.fuente: IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, casos_en («locative»), como adhikaraṇa 1 (tanda 1); Ñāṇamoli p. 7 («locative case») coincide

okāsa-kāraka.fuente: IEBH, como la anterior; Ñāṇamoli p. 7 («locative case», bajo okāsa)

okāra.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §511 («Why it is said “okāro” (the letter ‘o’)?»)

oṭṭhaja.en: (sound) produced at the lips; labial. The labials are 'u', 'ū'; 'p', 'ph'; 'b', 'bh'; 'm'.
oṭṭhaja.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 5 («labials (u, p, ph, b, bh, m)»)

opasilesikādhāra.en: locative of contact. E.g., in "mañce sayati", he sleeps on the bed, "mañce", on the bed, is called "opasilesikādhāra".

orasa.en: (sound) produced in the chest; pulmonary. It refers to the letter 'h' when it is associated with any of the nasals ('ṅ', 'ñ', 'ṇ', 'n', 'm') or with 'y', 'r', 'l', 'v'. Otherwise the letter 'h' is guttural.

kaṇṭha.en: the throat. One of the six places of articulation (ṭhāna).
kaṇṭha.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §13, nota a «dissimilar» («pronounced in the throat (kaṇṭha)»; «places of articulation»)

kaṇṭhaja.en: (sound) produced in the throat; guttural. The gutturals are 'a', 'ā'; 'k', 'kh'; 'g', 'gh'; 'ṅ'; 'h'.
kaṇṭhaja.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 5 y 14 («gutturals (a, k, kh, g, gh, ṅ, h)»); «throat» es N-EN, como kaṇṭha

kaṇṭha-tāluja.en: the letter 'e'; produced in the throat and the palate; gutturo-palatal.

kaṇṭhoṭṭhaja.en: the letter 'o'; produced in the throat and the lips; gutturo-labial.

kattu.fuente: N-EN, Kibbidhāna §548 («Also in the agent, instrument and place», glosando «Kattu-karaṇa-padesesu ca»)

kattu-kāraka.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («Active (kattu)», «active voice»); Ñāṇamoli p. 8 («active voice», bajo kattukāraka) coincide

kathitakamma.en: lit., spoken object; direct object. It refers to the primary object. When the verb has two objects (dvikammaka). E.g., in the sentence, "Bhagavā bhikkhū etad avoca", the Blessed One said this to the bhikkhus, "etad", this, is called kathitakamma, direct object, and "bhikkhū", akathitakamma, indirect object.
kathitakamma.nota: «el Bienaventurado» se da como «the Blessed One», como en akathitakamma (decisión del IEBH, sesión 58). El español corta la frase en «Se refiere al objeto primario. Cuando el verbo tiene dos objetos (dvikammaka).»; se respeta el punto.

kamma.en: object; that which receives the action of an active verb (the direct object).
kamma.fuente: N-EN, Kibbidhāna §524 («When there is an object which is at the beginning», glosando «Dhātuyā kammādimhi ṇo»); Ñāṇamoli p. 14 («object of word»)

kamma-kāraka.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («Passive (kamma)», «passive voice»); Ñāṇamoli p. 8 («passive voice», bajo kammakāraka) coincide

kammadhāraya.en: adjectival compound in which an adjective and a noun are combined. There are nine classes: (1) visesanapubbapada, (2) visesanuttarapada, (3) visesanobhayapada, (4) upamānuttarapada, (5) sambhāvanāpubbapada, (6) avadhāraṇapubbapada, (7) nanipātapubbapada, (8) kupubbapada, (9) pādipubbapada.
kammadhāraya.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 14 («adjectival compound [adj. + subs.]», «adjectival compound»)

kammapada.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 8 («passive», bajo kammapada); «passive voice» es IEBH, como kamma-kāraka

kammappavacanīya.en: name of certain prefixes (pari, pati, anu, abhi). The ending of these prefixes is in the second inflection (accusative) although the meaning may be in the sixth inflection (genitive), seventh (locative), etc. The definition of this term is "kammaṃ kiriyaṃ pavuttavanto ti kammappavacanīya", those that have indicated action are called "kammappavacanīya". This means that these prefixes no longer indicate the action and indicate something else: (1) mark (lakkhaṇa), (2) connection (sahattha), (3) inferior (hina). E.g., (1) "pabbajitam anu pabbajiṃsu", they went forth in imitation of the one who went forth (Buddha); (2) "nadim anu avasiṭṭhā Bārāṇasī", Varanasi is situated along the river; (3) "anu Sāriputtaṃ paññavā", the wise one is inferior to Sāriputta.
kammappavacanīya.termino: kammappavacanīya (prefixes that no longer indicate the action)
kammappavacanīya.nota: «renunciaron en imitación del renunciante» (pabbajiṃsu, pabbajitaṃ) se da como «went forth … the one who went forth», como pabbaji en anādara (tanda 1); si IEBH prefiere el calco «renounced», se cambia. «hina» va como lo imprime el Glosario (sin macrón; ¿por hīna?): no se enmienda.

karaṇa|1.en: the third case; the instrumental case. Also called tatiyā, karaṇa-vacana, sahayoga.
karaṇa|1.fuente: IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, casos_en («instrumental»), como apādāna (tanda 2); Ñāṇamoli pp. 7 y 14 («instrumental (tatiyā: third)», «instrumental case», bajo karaṇavacana) coincide

karaṇa|2.en: instrument of articulation; organ of articulation. The instruments of articulation are four: (1) the middle of the tongue (jivhāmajjha), for the palatals; (2) the curve of the tongue (jivhopagga), for the cerebrals; (3) the tip of the tongue (jivhāgga), for the dentals; and (4) its own place (sakaṭṭhāna).
karaṇa|2.fuente: traducción; «with the middle of the tongue in proximity with the palate» es N-EN, Sandhi §13, nota a «dissimilar»

karaṇa-vacana.fuente: IEBH, como karaṇa 1; Ñāṇamoli p. 14 («instrumental case», bajo karaṇavacana)

ka-vagga.fuente: traducción; N-EN, Sandhi §7, da «grouped» para vaggā (memo §2.1); Ñāṇamoli pp. 5 y 14 da «ka class (ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa)»

kāraka.en: that which performs the action. The ability to perform an action. Case; syntax. In the ancient grammars there are six: (1) kattu-kāraka, (2) kamma-kāraka, (3) karaṇa-kāraka, (4) sampadāna-kāraka, (5) apādāna-kāraka, (6) okāsa-kāraka. Both in Pāḷi and in Sanskrit the genitive is not called "kāraka". For a component of the sentence to be called "kāraka" it must have a direct connection with the verb or the action. In the sentences "puriso gacchati", the man goes, and "gāmaṃ gacchati", he goes to the village, both "puriso" and "gāmaṃ" are in connection with the verb and therefore are "kāraka". But in the sentence "purisassa gāmaṃ gacchati", he goes to the man's village, the genitive word "purisassa" is not in connection with the verb and therefore is not considered "kāraka". In the ancient grammars nominal inflections (nāma-vibhatti) are afterwards assigned to the six "kārakas". The nominal inflections or cases are eight: (1) nominative (paṭhamā, paccatta), (2) accusative (dutiyā, upayoga) (3a) ablative of agent, (tatiyā) (3b) ablative of instrument (karaṇa), (4) dative (catutthī, sampadāna), (5) ablative (pañcamī, nissakka, apādāna), (6) possessive or genitive (caṭṭhī, sāmī), (7) locative (sattamī, bhumma, adhikaraṇa), (8) vocative (ālapana).
kāraka.fuente: traducción; Ñāṇamoli pp. 8 y 15 («voice», «voice (of verb); syntax») coincide en «syntax»; los nombres de los casos son IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, casos_en
kāraka.nota: Ñāṇamoli da para kāraka «voice (of verb); syntax», y el Glosario «caso; sintaxis» (la voz la dan kattu-kāraka y kamma-kāraka). El Glosario llama «ablativo de agente» y «ablativo de instrumento» a los dos usos del tercer caso (tatiyā), que la norma de los paradigmas llama instrumental; se traduce tal cual («ablative of agent», «ablative of instrument»), sin enmendar, y lo mismo itthambhūta-vacana («ablative of likeness», que es también la palabra de Ñāṇamoli p. 7). «caṭṭhī» (por chaṭṭhī) y la puntuación «(3a) ablativo de agente, (tatiyā)» van como en el impreso.

kāraṇa.fuente: traducción; «particle» para nipāta es N-EN, Sandhi §51 (memo §2.1)

kāraṇa-vekalla.en: deficiency of causes; one of the uses of the verbal tense kālātipatti.
kāraṇa-vekalla.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («The non-occurrence of an action owing to a deficiency of causes (kāraṇavekalla)»)

kārita.en: causative. There are 4 causative suffixes: e, aya, āpe, āpaya.
kārita.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §523 («There is elision of the ‘ṇ’ of the causative») y §483 («In the causative»); IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («place the causative suffixes and assign the name “kārita”»); Ñāṇamoli p. 7 coincide
kārita.nota: N-EN, Ākhyāta §438, y comun/glosario.md (kārita: «sin traducir; equivalencia “causativo”») dan los cuatro sufijos con la ṇ indicadora: ṇe, ṇaya, ṇāpe, ṇāpaya. El Glosario los da sin ella (e, aya, āpe, āpaya); se traduce lo que dice el Glosario.

kāriya.en: the grammatical operation to be performed; substitution; change. See examples under kāriyī.
kāriya.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §517 («these operations are to be done», por kāriyāni); comun/glosario.md («operación gramatical») y glosario-ingles.json («grammatical operation») coinciden

kāriyī.en: That to which a certain type of grammatical operation is applied. In the aphorism "s' o" (Kac. §104), the ending 'si' is substituted by 'o'. Here 'si' is called kāriyī and 'o' kāriya. In the aphorism "sarā sare lopaṃ", vowels are elided owing to a following vowel, (Kac. §12), "sarā" (vowels) is called kāriyī, "sare" (owing to a following vowel) is called nimitta, and 'lopaṃ' (elision) is called kāriya.
kāriyī.termino: that to which a grammatical operation is applied
kāriyī.fuente: traducción; «is substituted by» y «elision» son N-EN, Sandhi §12, §17 y §44 (memo §2.1)

kāla.en: time; duration; measure. There are 3 verbal tenses: (1) past tense (atīta-kāla), (2) future tense (anāgata-kāla) and (3) present tense (paccuppanna-kāla).
kāla.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §413 («“kāla” (time)»); Ñāṇamoli p. 7 («tense»); los tres tiempos, como atīta-kāla y anāgata-kāla (tanda 1)

kālātipatti.en: conditional, conditional verbal tense. It expresses the future in relation to something that is past; and an action incapable of being performed owing to a certain difficulty during its execution. It is used to express (1) the non-occurrence of an action owing to a deficiency of causes (kāraṇavekalla) and (2) the non-occurrence of an action owing to the existence of conditions that prevent its realisation. (viruddhapaccayūpanipāta).
kālātipatti.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («Conditional (kālātipatti)»; los dos usos, «The non-occurrence of an action owing to a deficiency of causes (kāraṇavekalla) / The non-occurrence of an action owing to the existence of conditions that prevent its realisation»); Ñāṇamoli p. 7 coincide
kālātipatti.nota: comun/glosario.md fija kālātipatti como «sin traducir; acción pasada no ocurrida» (Ākhyāta, IEBH 2026-10-12) y glosario-ingles.json propone «not translated: action that has passed without happening»; N-EN, Ākhyāta §422, tampoco lo traduce («there is the inflection “kālātipatti”»). El Glosario dice «condicional», como la página del verbo ya adjudicada, y se sigue al Glosario. El español cierra con «. (viruddhapaccayūpanipāta).», paréntesis tras el punto; se reproduce así.

kālabyavadhāna.en: intervention of a period of time (metre). E.g., in the verse: "Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā ti, yadā paññāya passati; atha nibbindati dukkhe, esa maggo visuddhiyā" (Dh. 277); there is no euphonic combination (sandhi), between "passati" and "atha" owing to the intervention of a period of time ("atha" belongs to the line (pada) following "passati"). See byavadhāna.
kālabyavadhāna.termino: intervention of a period of time
kālabyavadhāna.fuente: traducción; Ñāṇamoli p. 5 lo define («a rest which prevents or resists sandhi», bajo kālavyavadhāna); «euphonic combination» para sandhi es glosario-ingles.json

kiṃ udāharaṇa.en: counter-example; exception to the rule. See sutta.

kita.en: name of the suffixes used to form primary derivatives (kitaka). The following suffixes belong to this category: nta, māna, ta, tavantu, tāvī, na, (ṇ)a, a, aka, ana, āvī, tu, (ṇ)ī, ra, tuṃ, tave, tvā, tvāna, tūna, ya, tya.
kita.fuente: N-EN, Kibbidhāna, título («Primary Derivative Chapter», «the primary derivative chapter (kita-kappa)»); el nombre queda sin traducir en §546 («The other suffixes are called “kit”»); comun/glosario.md, kitaka = «derivado primario»

kitanta-samāsa.en: a type of compound that has "kita", a primary derivative, as its last member. These compounds are fixed (nicca-samāsa), that is, their members cannot be separated. E.g., "kumbhakāro", potter.
kitanta-samāsa.termino: compound ending in a primary derivative
kitanta-samāsa.fuente: traducción; «primary derivative» es N-EN, Kibbidhāna, título
kitanta-samāsa.nota: El español imprime «nicca- samāsa», con espacio tras el guion; se une, que es errata de composición.

kicca.en: class of suffixes used to form primary derivatives (kitaka). They are passive participles. The following suffixes belong to this category: tabba, anīya, (ṇ)ya, (ṇ)iya, tayya, icca. The words formed with these suffixes are called future participles or potential passive participles.
kicca.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 8 y 12 («future passive participle»; «for formation of passive participles (suffixes = tabba, anīya, (ṇ)ya, (ṇ)iya, tayya, icca)»); N-EN, Kibbidhāna §545, deja el nombre sin traducir («are called “kicca”»)
kicca.nota: N-EN, Kibbidhāna §545, enumera cinco sufijos kicca: «tabba, anīya, ṇya, teyya, ricca». El Glosario da seis, con «tayya» e «icca» (la lista de Ñāṇamoli p. 12). Se traduce lo que dice el Glosario.

kitaka.en: primary derivative. These are formed directly from the roots by inserting a certain class of suffixes called kita.
kitaka.fuente: N-EN, Kibbidhāna, título («Primary Derivative Chapter»); comun/glosario.md (kitaka = «derivado primario», Samāsa, IEBH sesión 59) coincide

kitaka-nāma.en: primary nouns. Nouns formed using the primary suffixes kita.
kitaka-nāma.fuente: traducción, sobre «primary derivative» de N-EN (Kibbidhāna, título); Ñāṇamoli p. 6 da «derivative from verb» (bajo kitakanāma)

kiyādigaṇa.en: fifth conjugation group; group of roots beginning with "kī". The sign of this conjugation is 'ṇā'. The roots in this group are not numerous, totalling little more than 30.
kiyādigaṇa.termino: group of roots beginning with kī
kiyādigaṇa.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §449 («the group of roots that begin with ‘kī’»); IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («Group beginning with the root “kī” (kiyādi-gaṇa)»); Ñāṇamoli p. 8 («fifth conjugation (e.g. ki)»)
kiyādigaṇa.nota: N-EN, Ākhyāta §449 («there is the suffix ‘nā’»), y la página del verbo ya adjudicada («conjugational sign ‘nā’») escriben el signo sin la ṇ indicadora; el Glosario escribe 'ṇā', que es la forma de la derivación del propio N-EN («ki + ṇā + ti»). Se traduce lo que dice el Glosario. El español dice «quinto grupo conjugación», sin «de»; se traduce «fifth conjugation group».

kiriya.nota: Ñāṇamoli pp. 9 y 15 da para kiriya y kriyā «adverb, predicate», que es otra acepción; manda N-EN, que coincide con el Glosario.

kupubbapada-kammadhāraya.en: type of compound in which the first member is 'ku'. E.g., 'ku' + "putto" = "kuputto" (bad son).
kupubbapada-kammadhāraya.termino: adjectival compound whose first member is ku
kupubbapada-kammadhāraya.fuente: traducción; «adjectival compound» para kammadhāraya es de Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 14, como avadhāraṇapubbapada-kammadhāraya (tanda 2)

kriyā|1.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 9 y 15 («adverb, predicate»; «adverb, predicate of verb»)

kriyā-pada.en: lit., action-word; verb. It is a synonym of ākhyāta, verb.
kriyā-pada.fuente: IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («The verb · ākhyāta»), como ākhyāta (tanda 2)

kvaci.en: optionally; sometimes. Term frequently used in the aphorisms (sutta) to indicate that the rule has exceptions or only applies in some cases. Also navā and vā.
kvaci.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §14 ss. («sometimes»; memo §2.2); glosario-ingles.json coincide
kvaci.nota: comun/glosario.md fija kvaci → «a veces», vā → «opcionalmente» y navā → «ocasionalmente» (comun/terminologia-particulas.md), y N-EN las distingue igual: sometimes / optionally / occasionally. El Glosario da a kvaci «opcionalmente» en primer lugar y lo iguala a navā y vā; se traduce lo que dice el Glosario.

gaṇa.en: group; group of roots. Also dhātugaṇa.
gaṇa.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §450 («the group of roots», por dhātugaṇato); comun/glosario.md (dhātugaṇa = «grupo de raíces») y glosario-ingles.json («group of roots») coinciden; Ñāṇamoli p. 15 da «conjugation»

gamaka.en: the ability to express the meaning.
gamaka.termino: the ability to express the meaning

garu.en: strong (syllable). Syllables with a long vowel, syllables with the "niggahīta" and syllables with a short vowel followed by a double consonant are strong. E.g., "saṃsāra", cycle of rebirths; "datvā". In the first example, 'saṃ' is a strong syllable (garu) and so is 'sā'. In the second example, 'dat' and 'vā' are strong. See dīgha, long.
garu.nota: N-EN, Kibbidhāna §602 (nota), dice «heavy»: «Although ‘i’ is short (rasa), it is heavy (garu) and it has two moras»; y la pareja lahu va «light» en glosario-ingles.json (comun/glosario.md: lahu = «leve»). El Glosario español dice «fuerte», y aquí se sigue al Glosario; IEBH decide si el término va «heavy». Además el español imprime «"saṃsāra',» (comilla doble de apertura, simple de cierre) y «Veáse»; en inglés se cierra la comilla y se pone «See». Por esa comilla desparejada, la comprobación de ejemplos del generador empareja «saṃsāra', ciclo de renacimientos; » como cita y dará un aviso que no se puede evitar sin copiar español en el inglés.

gahādigaṇa.en: group of roots beginning with the root "gaha". The conjugational signs (vikaraṇa) are 'ppa' and 'ṇhā'. In some grammars this is an individual group (the sixth) while in others it is included in other groups.
gahādigaṇa.termino: group of roots beginning with gaha
gahādigaṇa.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §450 («the group of roots that begin with ‘gaha’»); IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («Group beginning with the root “gaha” (gahādi-gaṇa) — conjugational sign ‘ppa, ṇhā’»); «conjugational sign» para vikaraṇa es comun/glosario.md y glosario-ingles.json

guṇa.fuente: traducción; «strengthening» es el inglés de N-EN para vuddhi (Taddhita §352, «there is no (na) strengthening (vuddhi)»; comun/glosario.md); Ñāṇamoli p. 15 da «strong vowel gradation»

guṇa-nāma.en: adjective. Adjectives are declined like the nouns with which they must agree in gender, number and case. Also appadhānaliṅga, subordinate stem; vāccaliṅga, attributive stem; and visesana, distinguishing attribute.

ghosa.en: voiced (consonant). There are 21 voiced consonants: 'g', 'gh', 'ṅ'; 'j', 'jh', 'ñ'; 'ḍ', 'ḍh', 'ṇ'; 'd', 'dh', 'n'; 'b', 'bh', 'm'; 'y', 'r', 'l', 'v', 'h', 'ḷ'. According to Sad. iii §18, the grammarians of the Sanskrit language consider the "niggahīta" as voiced, but the grammarians of the Pāḷi language consider that it belongs neither to the group of the voiced nor to the group of the voiceless.
ghosa.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §9 («voiced / voiceless»; memo §2.1), como aghosa (tanda 1)
ghosa.nota: Ñāṇamoli p. 5 da «sonant, voiced»; manda N-EN, como en aghosa.

catutthī.en: the fourth case; the dative case. Also sampadāna.
catutthī.fuente: IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, casos_en («dative»); Ñāṇamoli pp. 7 y 15 («dative (catutthī: fourth)», bajo sampadānavacana; «dative case») coincide

catutthī-tappurisa.en: type of dependent determinative compound in which the first member has the fourth inflection. E.g., "saṃghassa" + "bhattaṃ" = "saṃghabhattaṃ", rice for the Order.
catutthī-tappurisa.termino: dependent determinative compound (first member in the fourth inflection)
catutthī-tappurisa.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 16 («dependent determinative compound»; «catutthītappurisa [dat. subs. + subs. or adj.]»); «inflection» para vibhatti es glosario-ingles.json
catutthī-tappurisa.nota: comun/glosario.md fija tappurisa = «compuesto determinativo» (Samāsa, IEBH sesión 59), sin «dependiente»; el Glosario dice aquí «dependiente determinativo», como Ñāṇamoli. Se traduce lo que dice el Glosario. «la Orden» va «the Order», como Gaṇa en el Sandhi inglés (memo §2.5).

catupadavibhāga.en: the four parts of speech. See vācogadhapada.
catupadavibhāga.fuente: traducción; «parts of speech» es Ñāṇamoli p. 17 (bajo padajāti)

ca-vagga.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §7 («grouped» para vagga; memo §2.1), como avagga (tanda 2); Ñāṇamoli p. 5 («ca class»)

curādigaṇa.en: the eighth group of roots; group of roots beginning with the root "cura". The conjugational signs of this conjugation (vikaraṇa) are 'ṇe' and 'ṇaya'. The initial consonant 'ṇ' indicates strengthening of the vowel of the first syllable of the root if it is not long or if it is not followed by two consonants.
curādigaṇa.termino: group of roots beginning with cura
curādigaṇa.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §452 («the group of roots that begin with ‘cura’, there are the suffixes ‘ṇe’ and ‘ṇaya’»); IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («Group beginning with the root “cura” (curādi-gaṇa)»); «strengthening» es N-EN (comun/glosario.md, vuddhi)

La página del verbo, ya adjudicada, escribe el signo «‘ṇe, naya’», sin la ṇ de naya, mientras N-EN §452 y el Glosario dan 'ṇaya': parece errata de la página del verbo, que IEBH puede querer corregir allí.

chaṭṭhī.en: the sixth case; the genitive (possessive) case. Also sāmī.
chaṭṭhī.fuente: IEBH, recursos/paradigmas/paradigmas.json, casos_en («genitive/possessive»); Ñāṇamoli pp. 7 y 15 («genitive (chaṭṭhī: sixth)», bajo sāmivacana; «genitive case») coincide
chaṭṭhī.nota: comun/glosario.md fija sāmī como «poseedor», sin el caso (IEBH 2026-10-08); el Glosario iguala chaṭṭhī y sāmī («También sāmī»). Se traduce lo que dice el Glosario.

chaṭṭhī-tappurisa.en: type of dependent determinative compound in which the first member is in the sixth inflection. It is the most common among the dependent determinative compounds. E.g., "rañño" + "putto" = "rājaputto", son of the king.
chaṭṭhī-tappurisa.termino: dependent determinative compound (first member in the sixth inflection)
chaṭṭhī-tappurisa.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 16 («dependent determinative compound»; «chaṭṭhītappurisa [gen. subs. + subs. or adj.]»)

jivhāmajjha.en: the middle of the tongue. One of the four instruments of articulation. See karaṇa 2.

jivhopagga.en: the arch of the tongue. One of the four instruments of articulation. See karaṇa 2.
jivhopagga.nota: El español imprime «karaṇa 2 .», con espacio antes del punto; se cierra, como en avyatta-sadda (tanda 2).

jha-saññā.en: the symbol 'jha'; the name 'jha'; it is used in the ancient grammars to designate masculine and neuter nominal stems (liṅga) ending in 'i', 'ī', verbs ending in 'i', 'ī', and the middle part of the nominal stem in 'i', 'ī'.
jha-saññā.nota: comun/glosario.md fija jha-saññā = «la designación «jha» (temas masculinos y neutros en -i, -ī)» y glosario-ingles.json propone «the designation «jha»». El Glosario dice «símbolo» y «nombre», y añade verbos y la parte media del tema; se traduce lo que dice el Glosario, sin juzgar el contenido. El español imprime «'ī"» (comilla simple de apertura, doble de cierre); se cierra con simple.

ṭa-vagga.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §7 («grouped» para vagga; memo §2.1), como avagga (tanda 2); Ñāṇamoli p. 5 («ṭa class»)

ṭhāna|1.en: place; place of articulation. There are six places of articulation: (1) the throat (kaṇṭha), (2) the palate (tālu), (3) the head (muddha), (4) the teeth (danta), (5) the lips (oṭṭha) and (6) the nose (nāsika).
ṭhāna|1.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §13, nota 19 («in different places of articulation»; «in the throat (kaṇṭha)»)

ṭhāna|2.en: word order in the sentence; position.
ṭhāna|2.nota: comun/glosario.md fija ṭhāna según el contexto: «causa» (taddhita, §356) o «lugar (apropiado)» (§401–§402); esta acepción del Glosario, orden de las palabras, no está en la norma.

ṭhānāsanna.en: proximity of the place of articulation.
ṭhānāsanna.termino: proximity of the place of articulation

ḍhakāra.fuente: N-EN, Kibbidhāna §612 («Why it is said ‘ḍhakāre’ (when the letter ‘ḍha’ follows)?»)

tagguṇasaṃviññāṇa.en: type of relative compound (bahubbīhi) in which what qualifies the meaning is brought along when the meaning of the other word (aññapada) is brought. What qualifies the meaning is included in the meaning of the other word. E.g., "lambakaṇṇaṃ ānaya", bring (the man who has) long ears. Here, what qualifies, long ears, is brought when the man is brought. It is the opposite of atagguṇasaṃviññāṇa.
tagguṇasaṃviññāṇa.termino: (relative compound) in which the qualifier is brought along
tagguṇasaṃviññāṇa.nota: «oreja larga» (singular genérico en español) se da como «long ears», que es lo natural en inglés; si el IEBH prefiere el calco «a long ear», se cambia.

tatiyā.en: the third case; the instrumental case. Also karaṇa.
tatiyā.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 15 («instrumental case», bajo tatiyā); N-EN, Uṇādi («In the instrumental (karaṇe)») coincide
tatiyā.nota: comun/glosario.md (Kāraka, IEBH 2026-10-08) fija karaṇa como nombre del kāraka, «caso del instrumento», y advierte que un kāraka no equivale a un caso. El Glosario identifica aquí tatiyā con karaṇa («También karaṇa»); se traduce tal cual y el IEBH decide si hace falta precisarlo.

tatiyā-tappurisa.en: type of dependent determinative compound in which the first member is in the third inflection. E.g., "Buddhena" + "desito" = "Buddhadesito", preached by the Buddha.
tatiyā-tappurisa.termino: dependent determinative compound (in the third inflection)
tatiyā-tappurisa.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 16 («dependent determinative compound» para tappurisa; tatiyātappurisa «[instr. subs. + subs. or adj.]», p. 10); «inflection» para vibhatti es glosario-ingles.json y N-EN, Uṇādi §626 («the second inflection»)

taddhita.en: secondary derivative. It is not derived directly from the root but from a primary derivative, kitaka.
taddhita.fuente: N-EN, título del capítulo 5 («Secondary Derivative Chapter»); Ñāṇamoli p. 16 («secondary derivative substantive»)
taddhita.nota: glosario-ingles.json (propuesta sin adjudicar) da todavía taddhita → «nominal derivative», cuando comun/glosario.md ya fija «derivado secundario» (IEBH, sesión 59) y N-EN dice «secondary derivative». Convendría alinear la propuesta, como se avisó en atthyattha-taddhita (tanda 1).

taddhita-nāma.en: secondary noun; a noun that is a secondary derivative.
taddhita-nāma.fuente: traducción; «secondary derivative» es N-EN, título del capítulo 5
taddhita-nāma.nota: Ñāṇamoli p. 6 da taddhitanāma «derivative from noun», que es otra definición (derivado de un nombre), no otra palabra. Se sigue al Glosario.

tanādigaṇa.en: the seventh group of roots; group of roots that begins with the root "tanu". The signs of this conjugation (vikaraṇa) are 'o', 'yira'.
tanādigaṇa.termino: seventh group of roots; group of roots that begins with “tanu”
tanādigaṇa.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §451 («After the group of roots that begin with ‘tanu’ there are the suffixes ‘o’ and ‘yira’»); IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json, tabla de los grupos, n.º 7 («Group beginning with the root “tanu” / (tanādi-gaṇa)»; «conjugational sign / (vikaraṇa)»)
tanādigaṇa.nota: Ñāṇamoli p. 8 numera tanādigaṇa como «sixth conjugation»; N-EN, la página del verbo (IEBH) y el Glosario lo dan como el séptimo grupo. Manda N-EN/IEBH; se deja constancia.

tappurisa.en: dependent determinative compound in which the first member is a noun, in any inflection except the first (that of the nominative or the vocative), explaining or determining the second member. There are six classes: (1) in the second inflection (dutiyā-tappurisa), (2) in the third inflection (tatiyā-tappurisa), (3) in the fourth inflection (catutthī-tappurisa), (4) in the fifth inflection (pañcamī-tappurisa), (5) in the sixth inflection (chaṭṭhī-tappurisa) and (6) in the seventh inflection (sattamī-tappurisa).
tappurisa.nota: comun/glosario.md (Samāsa, IEBH sesión 59) fija tappurisa → «compuesto determinativo», sin «dependiente», y la tanda 2 (amādi-tappurisa) dio «determinative compound» porque allí el Glosario dice sólo «determinativo». Aquí el Glosario dice «compuesto dependiente determinativo» y se traduce entero; el IEBH decide si el inglés se uniforma.

ta-vagga.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 5 («ta class (ta, tha, da, dha, na)», bajo tavagga); «grouped» para vagga es N-EN, Sandhi §7 (memo §2.1)

tāluja.en: produced in the palate; palatal. The palatals are 'i', 'ī'; 'c', 'ch'; 'j', 'jh'; 'ñ'; 'y'.
tāluja.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 5 («palatals (i, c, ch, j, jh, ñ, y)»)

tipada.en: one of the 9 classes of relative compounds (bahubbīhi). It consists of 3 members. E.g., "sīhassa pubbaddhaṃ viya kāyo assa iti sīhapubbaddhakāyo", his body is like the front part of a lion, therefore he is called one whose body is like the front part of a lion. This relative compound is formed by 3 members: (1) "sīha", lion, (2) "pubbaddha", front part, and (3) "kāya", body.
tipada.fuente: traducción; «relative compound» para bahubbīhi es de Ñāṇamoli pp. 11 y 17 y de glosario-ingles.json

tīṇi-liṅgāni.en: the three genders: (1) masculine (pulliṅga), (2) feminine (itthiliṅga) and (3) neuter (napuṃsakaliṅga).
tīṇi-liṅgāni.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 6 («tīṇi liṅgāni: 3 genders», bajo liṅga); «masculine / feminine / neuter gender», misma página

tumanta.en: lit., that ends in 'tuṃ'; the infinitive.
tumanta.nota: El español imprime «temina» (sic, por «termina»); se traduce «ends», que es errata de composición.

tumanta-pada.en: words that end in "tuṃ"; words in the infinitive.
tumanta-pada.fuente: traducción; «infinitive» para tumanta es de Ñāṇamoli p. 8

tumicchattha.en: desiderative. This conjugation is used to express the desire to perform an action. The root is reduplicated and the suffix 'sa' is added to form the stem, which receives the endings of the first conjugation.
tumicchattha.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 16 («desiderative»), que coincide con el Glosario
tumicchattha.nota: N-EN, Ākhyāta §434, glosa «tumicchatthesu» como «in the meanings of wanting and to do»; comun/glosario.md (Ākhyāta, IEBH 2026-10-12) fija «significado de querer [hacer algo]» («El desiderativo») y glosario-ingles.json propone «meaning of wanting [to do something]». El Glosario da el nombre de la conjugación, «desiderativo», y se traduce lo que dice; el IEBH decide si el término inglés debe ser el de N-EN.

tulyādhikaraṇa.en: relation of agreement. All adjectival compounds (kammadhāraya) are tulyādhikaraṇa. Also samānādhikaraṇa.
tulyādhikaraṇa.fuente: traducción del español del Glosario; «adjectival compound» para kammadhāraya es de Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 14
tulyādhikaraṇa.nota: N-EN, Ākhyāta §410-412, glosa «tulyādhikaraṇa» como «that have the same locus», y comun/glosario.md (Samāsa, IEBH sesión 59) fija «que se refiere a la misma cosa / misma localización / mismo locus», espejando el inglés de Nandisena en cada pasaje. El Glosario dice «relación de concordancia» y se sigue al Glosario; el IEBH decide si el término inglés debe ser el de N-EN.

tulyādhikaraṇa-bahubbīhi.en: type of relative compound whose members are in the same inflection.
tulyādhikaraṇa-bahubbīhi.termino: relative compound whose members are in the same inflection
tulyādhikaraṇa-bahubbīhi.fuente: traducción del español del Glosario; «relative compound» para bahubbīhi es de Ñāṇamoli pp. 11 y 17 y de glosario-ingles.json
tulyādhikaraṇa-bahubbīhi.nota: comun/glosario.md (Samāsa, IEBH sesión 59, Kacc. §328) fija «compuesto relativo que tiene la misma localización», espejando el inglés de Nandisena en §328 («same location»). El Glosario define por la inflexión («en la misma inflexión») y se traduce lo que dice; el IEBH decide. La referencia impresa «Kac., §328» lleva una coma de más; no afecta al inglés.

tyādi.en: lit., those that begin with 'ti'. Name given to the verbal inflections (ākhyāta-vibhatti). See vibhatti. Cf. syādi.
tyādi.fuente: traducción; «verbal inflection» para ākhyāta-vibhatti es IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json («verbal inflections (ākhyāta vibhatti)»)

danta.en: tooth; one of the 6 places of articulation (ṭhāna 1).
danta.nota: El español imprime «(ṭhāna 1 )» con espacio antes del paréntesis; se cierra. El «1» remite al homónimo ṭhāna 1.

dantaja.en: produced at the teeth; dental. The dentals are 't', 'th', 'd', 'dh'; 'n'; 'l'; 's'.
dantaja.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 5 («dentals (t, th, dh, d, n, l, s)»)

dantoṭṭhaja.nota: La referencia «(Rū. §2)» va dentro del texto impreso de la entrada, no en refs; se conserva en el inglés porque es del español.

dabba.en: substance; entity. One of the three properties of the nominal stem (liṅgattha).
dabba.nota: Se traduce el español revisado por el IEBH (2026-09-27: «del tema nominal»; el impreso decía «del tema»). comun/glosario.md (Saddanīti, IEBH 2026-10-14) fija liṅgattha → «significado de la base»; el Glosario lo glosa aquí de otro modo y se sigue al Glosario.

dabbābhidhāna.en: appellation denoting entity or substance. It is a synonym of nāma.
dabbābhidhāna.fuente: traducción; «appellation» para abhidhāna, como en la tanda 2

digu.en: numerical determinative compound. This class of compound can be included in the adjectival compound (kammadhāraya). There are two classes: (1) collective (samāhāra-digu) and (2) non-collective (asamāhāra-digu).
digu.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 16 («numerical determinative compound»); «adjectival compound» para kammadhāraya, pp. 10 y 14
digu.nota: comun/glosario.md (Compuestos, IEBH 2026-10-17) fija samāhāra-digu / asamāhāra-digu → «compuesto numérico colectivo / compuesto numérico individual». El Glosario dice aquí «no-colectivo» y se traduce «non-collective», como en asamāhāra-digu (tanda 2); el IEBH decide si se uniforma con «individual».

diyaḍḍhamatta.en: one and a half units of measure; one and a half morae.

divādigaṇa.en: the third group of roots; group of roots that begins with the root "divu". The sign of this conjugation (vikaraṇa) is 'ya'.
divādigaṇa.termino: third group of roots; group of roots that begins with “divu”
divādigaṇa.fuente: N-EN, Ākhyāta §447 («After the group of roots that begin with ‘divu’ there is the suffix ‘ya’»); IEBH, recursos/verbo/ingles.json, tabla de los grupos, n.º 3 («Group beginning with the root “divu” / (divādi-gaṇa)»); Ñāṇamoli p. 8 («third conjugation») coincide

disantarāḷattha.en: one of the 9 classes of relative compounds (bahubbīhi). It refers to the intermediate points of the compass. E.g., "pubbassā ca dakkhiṇassā ca disāya yad anarāḷaṃ sā 'yaṃ pubbadakkhiṇā vidisā", that which is between the east and south directions, this is the intermediate direction of the southeast.
disantarāḷattha.termino: (relative compound) denoting an intermediate point of the compass
disantarāḷattha.nota: El ejemplo imprime «anarāḷaṃ», que parece errata por «antarāḷaṃ» (cf. el lema disantarāḷattha); se reproduce tal cual porque el ejemplo es del impreso y no se enmienda.

dīgha.fuente: N-EN, Sandhi §5 («long»; memo §2.1); glosario-ingles.json y Ñāṇamoli p. 4 («long (vowel or syllable)») coinciden

dutiyā.en: the second case; the accusative case. Also upayoga. See kāraka.
dutiyā.fuente: Ñāṇamoli p. 16 («accusative case», bajo dutiyā); N-EN, Uṇādi §626, dice «the second inflection» (dutiyāyaṃ vibhattiyaṃ), que es el «segundo caso» del Glosario

dutiyā-tappurisa.en: type of determinative compound in which the first member is in the second inflection. E.g., "gāmaṃ" + "gato" = "gāmagato", who has gone to the village.
dutiyā-tappurisa.fuente: traducción; Ñāṇamoli p. 10 («dependent determinative compound», con dutiyātappurisa y el mismo ejemplo: «gone to the village»)
dutiyā-tappurisa.nota: El español imprime «está la segunda inflexión», sin «en»; se traduce «is in», que es errata de composición. Aquí el Glosario dice sólo «determinativo» (en tatiyā-tappurisa, «dependiente determinativo»); se sigue cada entrada como está.

dvanda.en: copulative or aggregative compound. Two or more nouns associated with the conjunction 'ca' (and) can be joined by eliminating the conjunctions. There are two classes: (1) collective (samāhāra-dvanda) and (2) individual (asamāhāra-dvanda).
dvanda.fuente: Ñāṇamoli pp. 10 y 16 («copulative compound»); glosario-ingles.json (propuesta), idéntica

dvikammaka.en: bitransitive (verb); verb that has two objects. Bitransitive verbs are the verbs to ask (pucchati) and to bring or carry (āharati, harati), etc. E.g., "Bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchati", he asks the Blessed One a question; here question (pañhaṃ) and Blessed One (Bhagavantaṃ) are in the second inflection and are objects (kamma) of the verb. Also sakammaka.
dvikammaka.nota: «También sakammaka» se traduce «Also sakammaka», como lo imprime el Glosario; pero el propio Glosario define sakammaka como «verbo transitivo» y remite de allí a dvikammaka. No es sinónimo estricto: el IEBH decide si debe leerse «Cf.» o «V.». «el Bienaventurado» → «the Blessed One», como en la tanda 1.

dvipada-tulyādhikaraṇa.en: one of the 9 classes of relative compounds (bahubbīhi). It consists of two members that refer to the same thing and are in the same inflection. There are 6 classes of this compound.
dvipada-tulyādhikaraṇa.termino: two-member (relative compound) referring to the same thing
dvipada-tulyādhikaraṇa.fuente: traducción; «that refer to the same thing» coincide con comun/glosario.md (tulyādhikaraṇa, «que se refiere a la misma cosa», Kacc. §324)

dvipada-bhinnādhikaraṇa.en: one of the 9 classes of relative compounds (bahubbīhi). It consists of two members which, before forming the compound, have different inflections. E.g., "chattaṃ pāṇimhi assa iti chattapāṇi puriso", there is an umbrella in his hand, so he is a man with an umbrella in his hand. Here, "chatta", umbrella, and "pāṇi", hand, before forming the compound have different inflections.
dvipada-bhinnādhikaraṇa.nota: comun/glosario.md (Samāsa, IEBH sesión 59) fija bhinnādhikaraṇabahubbīhi → «compuesto relativo que no tiene la misma localización». El Glosario define por las inflexiones y se traduce lo que dice; el IEBH decide.

dvimattā.en: two units of measure; two morae (the vowels 'ā', 'ī', 'ū', 'e', 'o'). Also dīgha, long. See mattā and accharāsaṅghāta.

dvebhāva.en: lit., state of two; doubling of a consonant when it is preceded by a vowel or in other cases. E.g. "idha" + "pamādo" = "idha ppamādo", here negligence. Also dvibhāva.
dvebhāva.nota: comun/glosario.md (Ākhyāta, IEBH 2026-10-12, Kacc. §458) fija dvebhāva → «reduplicación» (de la sílaba inicial de la raíz) y glosario-ingles.json propone «reduplication». Esta entrada del Glosario trata de la duplicación de consonante del Sandhi, para la que N-EN dice «doubling». El IEBH decide si el término va según contexto, como liṅga.

dhanita.en: aspirated (consonant). The second and fourth letters of each group are aspirated: 'kh', 'gh'; 'ch', 'jh'; 'ṭh', 'ḍh'; 'th', 'dh'; 'ph', 'bh'. Cf. sithila.

dhātu.en: it means an essential and basic element of the word. It is defined as that which ‘maintains’ its own meaning and also the meaning of others. Since the root is an essential and basic element of the word, most words in Pāḷi and also in Sanskrit are formed from a root and a suffix (paccaya). The word "dhātu" is formed from the root ‘dhā’ and the suffix ‘tu’. The words "pacati", "paccati", "pacīyate", "pacita", "pakka", "pacituṃ", "pacitvā", "pacanta", "pacamana", all these words are formed from the root "paca", to cook, with different suffixes and endings.
